messages.subject: problem with Firma tags
parts:
Hi,
So I've been running my analysis with the new tagging functions and in
general they have worked well until I got to the firma model. They are
still cutting off the intermediate steps' tag (and I've patched -- I
only have to do that once, right?). They do keep the original tags on
my AffymetrixCelSet, but I think they would have done that before.
There are a number of tags that *are* copied, but maybe because I
copied the folder with the output results over from another machine,
so aroma.affymetrix thinks that's part of the project name so firma is
not cutting them off? However, those tags do seem to be considered
tags, so its hard to say.
Best,
Elizabeth

> tags, so its hard to say.

The FirmaModel takes a ProbeLevelModel as its input, call it 'plm'.
The getDataSet() method for FirmaModel returns the what
getDataSet(plm) returns, which is the input to the PLM, *not* the
output. That explains what you are observing.

So, instead of having FirmaModel carrying down tags from
getDataSet(plm), you wish to get the tags from getChipEffectSet(plm),
correct?

> Best,
> Elizabeth
>
> > path<-"C:\\Documents and Settings\\Elizabeth\\My Documents\\Research\\Exon Arrays\\aroma.affymetrix.work\\probeData\\Affy_tissue_comm,RBC,main,QN,ep\\HuEx-1_0-st-v2"
> > csNTissue <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromFiles(path)

FYI, you can easily create a Windows Shortcut called 'probeData/' in
your working directory pointing to "C:\\Documents and
Settings\\Elizabeth\\My Documents\\Research\\Exon

Arrays\\aroma.affymetrix.work\\probeData", so you can use the
location-independent construct:

csNTissue <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName("Affy_tissue_comm,RBC,main,QN,ep",
chipType="HuEx-1_0-st-v2")

Btw, that can will look in both rawData/ and probeData/.

/Henrik

messages.subject: Re: problem with Firma tags
parts:
Hi Henrik,
I think that it is better to carry the tags from
getChipEffectSet(plm). True, right now you *have* to run the RMA,
merged=T to have residuals or weights, so it's a bit redundant, but
conceivably there might be another model fitting that gave residuals
that you would use (or someone will use FIRMA very oddly on something
else). Also, I'd like the tags to carry through as a documentation of
the analysis, regardless if there doesn't seem to be a choice about
running a particular step. There's always the possibility that there
was a choice made by the user, like changing the cdf or rerunning
under different versions of something that the tags could indicate.
Thanks,
Elizabeth

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: problem with Firma tags
parts: Hi,

On Dec 13, 2007 2:22 PM, epurdom <epu...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Henrik,
> So is there no longer user-override on tags without inheriting the
> previous tags? (that's okay, just wanting to check if it was the
> planned function)? I was doing a workaround (I will update from the
> SVN shortly) and tried to manually set with all the tags, but it
> inherited some of the tags from intensity dataset:

I may/may not understand what you want. So, basically here is the
format that getTags() returns:

<output tags> := <input data set tags>,<constructor tags>

where <constructor tags> defaults to "*" (argument 'tags' in
constructor). There is currently no way to override/remove the <input
data set tags>, but only the <constructor tags>. So, please don't
change the above rule/defintion, because that is a general pattern of
aroma.affymetrix.

For clarification, if specifying an asterisk in <constructor tags>,
e.g. tags="*,main", the asterisk tag is replaced with what
getAsteriskTags() is return. The latter returns tags that specify the
transform/model plus its parameters, e.g. for RmaCnPlm(...,
combineAlleles=TRUE, tags="*,foo") we get "RMA,A+B" from
getAsteriskTags() and "foo" from the remainder, such that:

<constructor tags>="RMA,A+B,foo"

in the above.

>
> > firmaTissue <- FirmaModel(plmTissue,tag="RBC,main,QN,ep,RMA,merged,ensb,ep,FIRMA,ep")

> FirmaModel:

>
> Instead, this workaround worked:

But with the new FirmaModel.R on the SVN that committed, you can use:

> firmaTissue <- FirmaModel(plmTissue,tag="*,ep")
> print(firmaTissue)
FirmaModel:
Data set: Affymetrix-HeartBrain
Chip type: HuEx-1_0-st-v2,core
Input tags: RBC,QN,RMA,merged

Isn't that what you want/wanted?
